title: Derived counit on a K-injective representative
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $u:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. In the categories of sheaves of constant-$R$ modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], assume the inverse image $u^{-1}$ is exact and left adjoint to $u_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Let $I$ be a K-injective complex on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Under the canonical comparison $u^{-1}Q(u_*I)\cong Q(u^{-1}u_*I)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] and the K-injective computation $Ru_*(QI)=Q(u_*I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], the counit of the canonical derived adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at $QI$ is represented by the ordinary sheaf counit $Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,I}):Q(u^{-1}u_*I)\to QI$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

source.place: Tag 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors) and Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors): the derived adjunction obtained from the underived one, whose counit at a complex where RF is computed by the complex itself (a K-injective complex, Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies) is the class of the underived counit; exact left adjoint computed termwise by Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: The cited module-sheaf adjunction supplies the required underived data: [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] says that the inverse image on constant-$R$ module sheaves is additive and exact and is left adjoint to $u_*$, while [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] identifies its counit on a sheaf with the componentwise sheaf counit $\varepsilon_{u,-}$. Applying the exact inverse image termwise to complexes therefore gives the derived inverse-image functor and its canonical comparison $u^{-1}Q(L)\cong Q(u^{-1}L)$ by [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor].

source.place: Tag 015F (derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor): an exact functor is computed termwise on all complexes; module adjunction data are the cited project definitions

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the module direct image $u_*$ is additive, so applying it termwise commutes with shifts and carries the cone of a chain map $a$ to the cone of $u_*(a)$; hence $Q\circ u_*$ is an exact functor on the homotopy category, and [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist] supplies K-injective resolutions in $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{et}},R)$. These are the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], which gives the derived-functor comparison $\gamma_I:Q(u_*I)\to Ru_*(QI)$ and says that it is an isomorphism because $I$ is K-injective; this is the computation $Ru_*(QI)=Q(u_*I)$ used in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] (resolution $1_{QI}$). Applying $u^{-1}$ and the comparison $\varphi$ of Step 1 identifies the source of the derived counit, $u^{-1}Ru_*(QI)\cong u^{-1}Q(u_*I)\cong Q(u^{-1}u_*I)$.

source.place: Tag 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies): K-injective complexes compute the right derived functor; Tag 015F for the exact inverse image

proof.text:
By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ on module sheaves with $u^{-1}$ exact and both functors additive, the counit being the sheaf counit $\varepsilon_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $u_*I$ is K-injective, and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] makes the termwise functors adjoint on the homotopy categories, with counit the class of the chain map $\varepsilon^0_{u,I}=(\varepsilon_{u,I^r})_r:u^{-1}u_*I\to I$ and inverse bijection $[g]\mapsto[\varepsilon^0_{u,I}\circ u^{-1}(g)]$. For a complex $N$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, the canonical derived Hom bijection of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at the K-injective target $QI$ is the composite of natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(u^{-1}QN,QI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(Q(u^{-1}N),QI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(u^{-1}N,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(N,u_*I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(QN,Q(u_*I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(QN,Ru_*QI),$$
where $K$ denotes homotopy categories: the first is precomposition with $\varphi_N^{-1}$ (Step 1), the second and fourth are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for the K-injective targets $I$ and $u_*I$, the third is the homotopy adjunction, and the fifth is composition with $\gamma_I$ (Step 2). This is the colimit description of the canonical derived adjunction (Stacks 0FND) in which, the target being K-injective and the left adjoint exact, the indexing quasi-isomorphisms may be taken to be identities; no boundedness is used. Following an element through the chain, for a chain map $a:N\to u_*I$ the morphism $\gamma_I\circ Q(a)$ corresponds to $Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,I}\circ u^{-1}(a))\circ\varphi_N$. The transpose of $h:QN\to Ru_*QI$ is $\varepsilon_{u,QI}\circ u^{-1}(h)$; taking $N=u_*I$ and $a=1$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{u,QI}\circ u^{-1}(\gamma_I)=Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,I})\circ\varphi_{u_*I}.$$
Since $u^{-1}(\gamma_I)$ and $\varphi_{u_*I}$ are the identifications of Step 2, this says that the derived counit at $QI$ is represented by $Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,I}):Q(u^{-1}u_*I)\to QI$, as claimed.
